label: original-phase input of 0/m/z/b/u/w/q after a y/j/k/e-type prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.8% of mass), never at t=0, and peaks at positions 2-4 (t=3 alone carries 36% of mass). It is nearly silent at the delimiter and during copying. The input token matters most: 0, m, z, b, u, w, q (0/m/z have about 5-6x lift), mostly on their first occurrence (95% of mass). Recent context modulates it: the strongest activations come right after e/q/t/f, two steps after y/j/a/k, or in sequences that start with y or k. Typical top cases are "y e 0", "j e z", "c e m". The input token alone gives high recall but low precision (about 9%), because the same tokens with other prefixes stay below threshold. That points to a graded, distributed dependence on the hidden state that a simple predicate does not capture. The chosen predicate gets dev F1 0.32 with mass recall 0.59. Many weaker activations fall outside it, e.g. p and f inputs, and repeated tokens late in the sequence.
